Title: MACC submits several governance improvement recommendations to Felda, two subsidiaries
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has submitted several governance improvement recommendations to the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and two of its subsidiaries to enhance transparency in the implementation of the Agro Park (Commercial) Project and the Cattle Trading Pilot Project.
MACC said that these recommendations were presented through its Governance Investigation Division to Felda, FIC Supplies Sdn Bhd, and FIC Integrated Property Management (FIC IPM).
Among the recommendations put forward is the restructuring of FIC IPM's role as an independent advisory panel to ensure that the views and advice provided are more objective, transparent, and free from conflicts of interest, MACC said in a Facebook post today.
MACC also recommended that Felda establish specific standard operating procedures (SOPs) for procurement through Requests for Proposal and variation orders, and improve FIC Supplies' transaction procedures to strengthen internal controls and transparency.
"Felda and its subsidiaries welcome the recommendations and have committed to implementing them in stages," according to the post.
According to MACC, agreement on these recommendations was finalised through a Governance Improvement Report signed by Felda deputy director-general of Services Muhammad Fitri Othman, FIC Group chief executive officer Syed Fadil Syed Sofi, and MACC Governance Investigation Division Director Datuk Mohazaki Hassan.

Title: IHH says Fortis stake acquired via transparent, widely public competitive bidding
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IHH Healthcare Bhd said its position remained that its subsidiary, Northern TK Venture Pte Ltd (NTK), acquired its stake in Fortis Healthcare in 2018 through a transparent, widely public and fully regulated competitive bidding process.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the healthcare group said the transaction obtained all necessary corporate, shareholder and regulatory approvals, including those required under the Competition Commission of India (CCI) and the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) takeover regulations.
"IHH's investment was made through a preferential allotment of newly issued Fortis shares amounting to INR4,000 crore for a 31 per cent stake, together with a mandatory tender offer to the public shareholders.
"No secondary shares were acquired from the former promoters and judgement debtors, Malvinder Mohan Singh and Shivinder Mohan Singh, and no payments were made to them," it said in a statement.
The statement comes after the Supreme Court of India on Sept 25, 2026 disposed of a Special Leave Petition (SLP) filed by Fortis challenging a Delhi High Court's order requiring a forensic audit in relation to the company.
IHH said it will fully cooperate with the forensic audit and is confident that an independent review will objectively establish the facts surrounding the transaction.

Title: 'Maha' for Mahathir, Hasmah: Alor Setar clinic stands as lasting tribute to late couple
Article:
ALOR STAR: Maha Klinik, a fixture here since 1957, stands as a testament to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad's enduring love for his late wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali.
Administrative assistant Mercy Samuel, 69, who has worked at the clinic for nearly 50 years, said its unique name was more than a medical brand, as it combined the names Mahathir and Hasmah.
"They met while studying together in Singapore. After they completed their studies and married, Tun Dr Mahathir decided to leave public service to open his own clinic.
"As a token of his love for his beloved wife, who was always by his side and a source of inspiration, he immortalised the combination of their names on the Maha Klinik signboard," she told reporters at the clinic today.
She said Maha Klinik opened in Pekan Melayu in 1957 before moving to Jalan Sultan Badlishah in 1979.
To this day, it remains associated with the names of Tun Dr Mahathir and Tun Dr Siti Hasmah.
"Tun Dr Mahathir handed over the clinic to Datuk Dr Mohamed Yacob Dawood around the late 1970s. Whenever the couple returned to Alor Setar, they would come by and ask after everyone.
"Every Ramadan, they never failed to invite the clinic staff to break fast together at their niece's or nephew's home in Alor Setar. The late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah was always by Tun Dr Mahathir's side, wherever he went," she said.
[[nid:1543213]]
Mercy said Dr Siti Hasmah's passing had deeply affected the clinic's staff, describing her as a humble and maternal figure who was loved by people from all walks of life.
Meanwhile, Maha Klinik medical officer Dr Reshampreet Kaur, 39, said Dr Siti Hasmah was a pioneer in several areas of medicine, including family planning and maternal and child health.
She said the couple had also provided free or low-cost treatment to people in rural areas and those from underprivileged backgrounds.
"From the very beginning, if Tun Dr Mahathir saw someone struggling come to the clinic, he would not charge them, or would charge very little. That is something we have kept to this day, charging only low fees.
"Even after Tun Dr Mahathir stopped treating patients to enter politics, this clinic continued to operate and is remembered by the people of Kedah. Even now, some people come to the clinic just to take a photo of the Maha Klinik signboard," she said.

Title: Special delivery: India state hands out gold for newborns
Article:
MADURAI: Authorities in India's Tamil Nadu state gave babies born in government-run hospitals a free gold ring on Monday, an initiative aimed at boosting confidence in the public healthcare system.
Under the scheme launched by actor-turned-Chief Minister Vijay, all babies born in public health facilities in the state are eligible for a one-gram gold ring, worth some US$143.
Gold has immense cultural significance in India, featuring prominently in weddings and religious ceremonies, and is seen as a safe generational asset.
"The gold ring would give the child something valuable to keep for the years ahead," said one mother at a government hospital in the state's Madurai district, who declined to give her name.
She was among dozens of mothers who cradled their newborns as they queued up to receive the gift.
"This scheme feels personal," another grateful mother, Stella Mary, told AFP.
Officials say the initiative aims to highlight maternal and newborn care, while strengthening faith in public healthcare institutions in the southern state of over 72 million people.
The scheme, however, drew some criticism from the Bharatiya Janata Party, which is in the opposition in Tamil Nadu.
"A gold ring for a newborn may be a welcome gesture, but for families, the most immediate need is ensuring that essential nutrition is available every day," party member Tamilisai Soundararajan said in a social media post.
India's overcrowded public hospitals often struggle with staff shortages, long waiting times and patchy infrastructure, prompting many patients to seek treatment in the costly private sector.
While most women in India give birth in hospitals, home deliveries still occur in some rural communities, making institutional childbirth a priority for health authorities.
Despite significant gains in recent years, infant and maternal mortality rates continue to languish in India.
The country recorded 24 infant deaths per 1,000 live births while maternal deaths stood at 88 per 100,000 live births, according to latest official data.
The gold ring scheme, known as the "Thaimaman" (maternal uncle) programme, draws on the special cultural significance of a child's maternal uncle, who is often expected to play a key role in family milestones and celebrations.
It also taps into India's enduring obsession with gold.
For many women, particularly in rural areas, gold jewellery can serve as a form of personal financial security.
India is one of the world's largest consumers of the metal. According to the World Gold Council, demand in the country reached US$25 billion in the first quarter of this year.

Title: Federal Court allows Pelorus to directly recover RM2.4mil from former partners
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court has ruled that a joint venture partner can directly sue its former business partners to recover money it claims had been misused or diverted.
A three-member panel led by Chief Justice Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh made the ruling in an appeal by Pelorus Holding Sdn Bhd against Jaffa Roger Dawkins, Rabiatul Adawiyyah Mohmad and Harris Luqman Group Sdn Bhd.
The other members of the bench were Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah and Datuk Azimah Omar.
The court held that Pelorus was entitled to enforce obligations owed directly to it under a joint venture agreement (JVA).
Pelorus had entered into the agreement with Dawkins and Rabiatul to establish a joint venture company involved in businesses including livestock supply, integrated farming and breeding, abattoir operations, and the supply of fresh and frozen meat products.
The relationship later deteriorated, with Pelorus claiming that the joint venture had not been managed according to the terms of the agreement.
Pelorus subsequently sued to recover several sums, including RM1.188 million, which it claimed had been diverted for the benefit of Harris Luqman Group, and RM1.213 million advanced to service the company's Agrobank loan.
The High Court allowed the claims.
However, the Court of Appeal later ruled that the two sums belonged to the joint venture company and that any claim should be brought by the company itself, either directly or through a derivative action.
A derivative action allows a shareholder to sue on behalf of a company where the company itself does not take action.
The Federal Court disagreed.
Wan Ahmad Farid said the joint venture company, Pelorus HLG Sdn Bhd, had already been incorporated when the JVA was signed on Aug 16, 2016.
"However, the parties had chosen not to make the company a party to the agreement.
"It was not a drafting oversight, but a clear demonstration of contractual intent," he said in the grounds of judgment dated Sept 21.
He said the parties had consciously chosen to bind themselves personally under the JVA.
Wan Ahmad Farid said Pelorus was not merely a shareholder complaining about losses suffered by the joint venture company.
Instead, he said Pelorus was seeking the return of its own money and enforcing rights arising directly from the JVA.
"The plaintiff is not an aggrieved shareholder complaining of a wrong done to its company, but a contracting party claiming its due under a binding JVA."
The court also said the fact that some of the money had passed through the joint venture company's accounts did not automatically mean the claim belonged to the company.
It said the key question was whose money had been advanced and to whom the obligation to repay it was owed.
The court also rejected an argument that the funding arrangements amounted to illegal moneylending.
It held that the advances were made as part of the commercial arrangements agreed under the JVA and were not separate moneylending transactions.
The Federal Court allowed Pelorus' appeal involving the RM1.188 million and RM1.213 million claims.
It also maintained Pelorus' RM1 million claim based on personal guarantees given by Dawkins and Rabiatul.
However, the court dismissed a separate RM516,972.02 claim after agreeing with the Court of Appeal that it had not been sufficiently substantiated.
The respondents were ordered to pay RM100,000 in costs.

Title: RM260mil UiTM funds channelled without MOF approval, PAC calls for stronger oversight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Almost RM260 million in funds channelled into Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Holdings entities and companies was not properly carried out as required under financial regulations and procedures, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) said.
PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the committee's findings confirmed that the RM260 million funding was channelled without obtaining the approval of the finance minister as required by law.
She said the findings were detailed in two PAC reports tabled in the Dewan Rakyat in 2024.
"PAC also found critical structural weaknesses in the oversight and corporate governance of the institution's investment management.
"These weaknesses require immediate improvements to ensure that all investment and expenditure decisions involving public funds strictly comply with legal guidelines and provide the best value for money," she said in a statement.
She said PAC had submitted detailed recommendations to the ministry and university administration to strengthen monitoring mechanisms, ensure full accountability and prevent weaknesses in financial governance from recurring.
She said MACC, which also serves as an ex-officio member of PAC, had demonstrated close and proactive cooperation in examining all aspects of the findings to ensure there were no elements of misappropriation, corruption or abuse of power.
"PAC will continue to carry out its oversight and check-and-balance role over the government to ensure transparency, accountability and integrity in the management of the country's finances."
The reports, titled DR. 3 Tahun 2024 and DR. 21 Tahun 2024, are available on the official PAC website.

Title: Impact Capital moves closer to ACE Market listing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Impact Capital Holdings Bhd has signed an underwriting agreement with Public Investment Bank Bhd (PIVB) ahead of its proposed listing on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market.
The IPO will comprise a public issue of 96.69 million new shares and an offer for sale of 28.62 million existing shares in Impact Capital, an ICT systems integrator focused on critical infrastructure.
Of the new shares, 24 million, or five per cent of the enlarged share capital, will be offered to Malaysian retail investors.
A total of 16 million shares, or about 3.33 per cent, will be allocated to eligible directors, employees and other contributors to the group.
Another 56.69 million new shares, representing about 11.81 per cent, will be placed with selected investors.
The offer for sale involves 28.62 million existing shares, equivalent to about 5.96 per cent of the enlarged share capital, through private placement.
Public Investment Bank Bhd will underwrite the 40 million shares allocated to the Malaysian public and eligible persons.
Impact Capital managing director Winston Chai Fung Chun said the underwriting agreement marked a major step towards the company's listing after more than two decades in the ICT industry.
The company provides ICT integration solutions for telecommunications infrastructure, enterprise networks, data centres, security systems and digital twin applications.
It also supplies ICT hardware and software and provides maintenance, support and managed network services.
Chai said the listing would support expansion of the company's operational footprint, workforce and business development capabilities, as well as technology investments, including a planned Digital Innovation and Solutions Centre.
PublicInvest chief executive officer Lee Yo-Hunn said Impact Capital's experience across critical infrastructure sectors provides a foundation for its next growth phase.
Proceeds from the IPO will be used to expand offices and workforce, fund business development, enhance technology capabilities, meet working capital needs and defray listing expenses.
PublicInvest is the principal adviser, sponsor, sole underwriter and sole placement agent for the IPO.

Title: Police, RTD turn up heat on road hooligans in Iskandar Puteri
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Police seized 43 motorcycles and issued 112 summonses in an operation targeting illegal street racing and road hooliganism at the Lima Kedai toll plaza near here, yesterday
The joint operation included federal Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department policemen and also state Road Transport Department officers.
Acting district police chief Superintendent Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said 57 motorists, including five women, aged between 15 and 30, were inspected.
Police issued 112 summonses, while RTD slapped offenders with106 notices for various offences, while 43 motorcycles were seized under Section 64 of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Saifullah said similar operations would be conducted continuously to curb illegal racing and maintain public safety and order in the district.

Title: Poh Kong FY26 net profit jumps 60pct to RM193.37mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Poh Kong Holdings Bhd's net profit rose 59.7 per cent to RM193.37 million for the financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY26), from RM121.10 million a year earlier.
Revenue increased to RM1.93 billion from RM1.69 billion, the jewellery retailer said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia today.
For the fourth quarter (Q4), net profit rose to RM36.20 million from RM22.68 million in the corresponding quarter last year, while revenue increased to RM378.36 million from RM365.50 million.
"The increase in revenue was due mainly to the surge in gold price during the quarter under review," it said.
Poh Kong said revenue was largely derived from its retail segment.
On its prospects, the group said Malaysia's economy remains well-positioned despite a more challenging global environment shaped by geopolitical tensions, softer external demand, inflation and currency fluctuations.
"We believe that strong central bank buying, consumer spending and safe-haven inflows amid global geopolitical uncertainties will continue to fuel demand for both jewellery and gold investment products," it said.
The group said it would continue to monitor the impact of current uncertainties on its operations, honour its financial obligations and evaluate its performance on an ongoing basis.
"Barring unforeseen circumstances, the group is confident that it has put in place adequate measures to meet the challenges ahead for the financial year ending July 31, 2027," it said.
Meanwhile, Poh Kong recommended a final single-tier dividend of 5.00 sen per ordinary share for FY26, up from 3.00 sen per share for FY25.
The proposed dividend, amounting to RM20.52 million, is subject to shareholders' approval at the forthcoming annual general meeting, it said.

Title: Mukhriz asks public to forgive Siti Hasmah, settle any outstanding debts
Article:
SERDANG: Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir today appealed to members of the public to forgive any wrongdoings or mistakes committed by his late mother, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, during her lifetime.
Speaking after funeral prayers for Dr Siti Hasmah at Masjid As Syarif, Taman Sungai Besi Indah, Mukhriz also asked anyone with claims involving outstanding debts owed by his mother to contact the family.
He said the family would do its best to settle any debts left by Dr Siti Hasmah.
"Should there have been any wrongdoings or mistakes on her part, please forgive her.
"Also, if there are any outstanding debts, please deal with us, the family. God willing, we will settle them to the best of our ability," he said.
Mukhriz was speaking after more than 2,000 congregants gathered at the mosque for funeral prayers for Dr Siti Hasmah, who died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) at 9.20am today.
The funeral prayers were performed twice, with the first led by Ustaz Muhammad Danial Hussan and the second by family representative Ustaz Basyir.
The prayers were completed about 5.15pm, after which the remains were taken to the Presint 20 Muslim Cemetery in Putrajaya for burial under the State Funeral of a National Dignitary accorded by the government.
A sombre atmosphere prevailed at the mosque as family members, political leaders, friends and members of the public gathered to pay their final respects.
Among those present were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail; former prime ministers Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob; and Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan were also present.
Earlier, Anwar announced that Dr Siti Hasmah would be accorded a state funeral following her death.
The Prime Minister's Department subsequently announced that she would be accorded the State Funeral of a National Dignitary.
Dr Siti Hasmah, 100, was the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad. The couple had seven children, including Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir, Datuk Marina Mahathir, Mirzan Mahathir and Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir.
Anwar earlier described her death as a great loss to society and the nation, and urged those attending an event he was officiating to recite Al-Fatihah for her.

Title: Bursa Malaysia ends marginally lower amid lack of fresh catalysts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended marginally lower on Monday amid selling activity as the market lacked fresh catalysts to spur investors' buying interest, an analyst said.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 1.60 points, or 0.09 per cent, to 1,670.02, from Friday's close of 1,671.62.
The benchmark index, which opened 0.93 of-a-point higher at 1,672.55, moved between 1,668.61 and 1,674.11 throughout the trading session.
Market breadth was negative as losers surpassed gainers 748 to 388, while 517 counters were unchanged, 1,271 untraded and 91 suspended.
Turnover slipped to 3.11 billion units worth RM2.40 billion from 4.07 billion units valued at RM2.69 billion on Friday.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the stockbroking firm maintained a cautious view of the market as persistent external headwinds and foreign selling could limit near-term upside.
"Nevertheless, the recent market correction has brought valuations of selected blue-chip stocks to more attractive levels, which could encourage bargain hunting, particularly among fundamentally strong heavyweights.
"Hence, we expect trading to remain selective, with buying interest likely to emerge on further weakness," he told Bernama.
As such, he anticipated the FBM KLCI to trend within the 1,660-1,690 range for the week.
Berjaya Research Sdn Bhd head of research Kenneth Leong said market attention will also turn to US job openings and consumer confidence data due tomorrow, which could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's policy path and global risk appetite.
"A softer-than-expected set of readings may offer some relief to equities, but signs of resilient labour demand or weakening consumer sentiment could add to market volatility," he said.
Among the heavyweights, Maybank eased six sen to RM10.16, Public Bank fell one sen to RM4.79, CIMB added nine sen to RM7.99, Tenaga Nasional firmed two sen to RM13.16, and IHH Healthcare gained two sen to RM8.01.
In active trade, Zetrix AI was unchanged at 19 sen, Jaks Resources put on 1.5 sen to 18.5 sen, ACE Market debutant Evocom fell five sen to 13 sen, Aimax perked up half a sen to one sen, and Inari Amertron slid 11 sen to RM2.55.
Of the top gainers, Hong Leong Bank advanced 22 sen to RM23.36, Hong Leong Financial garnered 18 sen to RM18.90, Ayer Holdings increased 12 sen RM7.60, Grand Central jumped 11 sen to 42 sen, and Solarvest improved 10 sen to RM4.16.
Malaysian Pacific Industries led the losers list, falling RM1.98 to RM42.20, United Plantations lost 98 sen to RM31.60, Fraser & Neave erased 78 sen to RM22.22, Hong Leong Industries slipped 30 sen to RM16.66, and Kelington sank 27 sen to RM8.72.
On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index fell 157.14 points to 17,687.77, the FBM Emas Index retreated 41.85 points to 12,414.79, the FBM Top 100 Index reduced 36.51 points to 12,206.95, the FBM Emas Shariah Index slid 63.91 points to 12,242.32, and the FBM ACE Index dipped 42.25 points to 5,490.61.
Sector-wise, the Financial Services Index climbed 47.89 points to 19,598.38, the Industrial Products and Services Index shed 1.30 points to 182.80, the Energy Index eased 0.01 of-a-point to 861.82, and the Plantation Index slumped 116.38 points to 9,218.49.
The Main Market volume decreased to 1.69 billion units worth RM2.05 billion from 2.53 billion units valued at RM2.24 billion last Friday.
Warrants turnover trimmed to 944.79 million units worth RM156.45 million from 999.87 million units valued at RM180.99 million previously.
The ACE Market volume declined to 469.48 million units valued at RM190.74 million from 539.02 million units worth RM264.01 million on Friday.

Title: Azalina: Media freedom a key point in Freedom of Information Bill
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Media freedom is one of the key points in the proposed Freedom of Information (FOI) Bill 2026, says Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
The minister in the prime minister's department (law and institutional reform) said this was to ensure media practitioners had adequate space to report on matters of public interest.
She said the drafting of any new laws must not be restrictive or make it difficult for journalists to carry out their duties, as they are cornerstones of information transparency in a democratic country.
"For me, part of a country's democracy is having media freedom and ensuring that journalists have the full ability to carry out their work," she told reporters following a public hearing on the FOI Bill in Parliament.
Azalina said this was in line with Article 10 of the Federal Constitution concerning freedom of speech.
She said freedom of speech means little if the public and the media are denied basic access to accurate information.
"There is no point talking about freedom of speech under Article 10 if you do not have the information to speak about. If you do not speak up, what is there to convey?"
She said it would be inappropriate for a bill called the Freedom of Information Bill to ultimately serve merely as a law for controlling information.
"What's the point? So, it's better not to waste your time, our time and everyone else's.
"If you want to do it, then do it... if you don't, then don't," she said.
Azalina said the bill should not be drafted merely to ensure that Malaysia has a freedom of information law.
She said it should contain clear provisions concerning rights, exemptions, the responsibilities of authorities, as well as review and redress mechanisms.
She added that the public hearing, for example, provided an avenue for civil society, non-governmental organisations, students and the public to voice their views before a final position is reached.
"We (members of parliament) have all taken an oath that our priority is the people. That is why today (the public hearing) is so meaningful here in the Parliament building.
"We want to put the people first when it comes to matters involving information," she said.

Title: The wildfires choking Indonesia, sparking regional haze
Article:
JAKARTA: For weeks, Indonesia has been battling fires that have burned vast swathes of forest and peat ecosystems, causing toxic haze to blanket parts of the country, Malaysia and Singapore.
The fires have harmed humans and animals alike, and prompted criminal charges, licence suspensions and a presidentially mandated new agency to tackle fires in peat ecosystems.
Here's what to know:
What is the latest situation?
Between January and July alone, more than 202,000 hectares (780 square miles) were razed by fire, according to government figures. That is an area roughly three times the size of the capital Jakarta, and represents a 69 per cent increase in burned areas in the same period last year.
But the figures have not been updated since, and the burning has only worsened.
The Nusantara Atlas project, which uses satellite monitoring, estimates nearly 896,000 hectares – over five times the size of Greater London – had burned by the end of August.
South Papua province on the country's easternmost island was the most affected region, with more than 168,000 hectares burned as of August, according to Nusantara Atlas.
NGO Yayasan Pusaka Bentala Rakyat said fires have been detected inside a large-scale government food estate project in South Papua, local media reported.
What is causing the fires?
The El Nino weather phenomenon typically brings dry conditions to Indonesia, and this cycle is predicted to be among the strongest in decades and last until early 2027.
But experts said human factors are also key, including slash-and-burn land clearing and decades of forest degradation that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape.
"El Nino isn't actually the cause, but it's a trigger. There still needs to be an ignitor," IPB University forestry lecturer Ati Dwi Nurhayati told AFP.
"We know that in peatlands, almost 100 per cent (of the fires) was caused by human activity."
Peat ecosystems are dense layers of partially decomposed organic materials that are normally waterlogged. But in much of Indonesia they have been dried out so the land can be planted. This has created highly flammable regions.
Once peat catches fire, it can smoulder and reignite for days, making firefighting efforts complex.
[[nid:1543151]]
In the first eight months of this year, more than 212,000 hotspots have been detected inside peat ecosystems across the country, according to NGO Pantau Gambut.
The figure was more than double that recorded during 2015's strong El Nino.
What is the government's response?
Indonesia has deployed firefighters assisted by volunteers across affected areas, and used cloud seeding and water bombing, with limited success. Malaysia and Japan have also offered assistance.
Authorities revoked the permits of five companies accused of contributing to the fires, with dozens more frozen.
President Prabowo Subianto last week ordered the creation of a new government agency to manage tropical peat and mangrove ecosystems and carry out fire prevention.
Indonesia set up a similar agency after the 2015 fires, initially tasked with peat and expanded to mangroves in 2020. But its mandate was not renewed when it expired in 2024.
In 2015, fires burned more than two million hectares in Indonesia, costing an estimated US$16.1 billion in damages, according to the World Bank.
But the agency's establishment has been met with some scepticism.
"The important thing is to ensure that this agency's mandate can answer the issue of peat management, not just introduce a new structure," Pantau Gambut senior campaigner Putra Saptian said in a statement.
What are the impacts?
Indonesia's Health Ministry said last week that cases of respiratory illness have climbed past 170,000 in haze-hit provinces across Sumatra and Borneo.
The blazes have also had a devastating impact on wildlife.
Indonesian authorities have rescued 100 animals, including 53 orangutans, that were threatened by the blazes, a forestry ministry official said last week.
In Borneo, fires have been detected within habitats containing 52 per cent of the island's orangutan population, the International Union for Conservation of Nature said.
The haze has spread beyond Indonesia's border, drifting particularly into Malaysian Borneo's Sarawak state, where schools have periodically closed because of the smog.
It has also reached Singapore and even caused declining air quality in the Philippines and southern Thailand.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Siti Hasmah laid to rest at Putrajaya National Cemetery [WATCH]
Article:

accorded a state funeral
.

died at the National Heart Institute
(IJN) in Kuala Lumpur at 9.20am today.

Earlier, more than 2,000 congregants gathered at Masjid As Syarif for funeral prayers for Dr Siti Hasmah.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, had also
expressed their condolences
over her passing.

remembered for her decades of service

Title: Penang governor, CM extend condolences over Siti Hasmah's passing
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Ramli Ngah Talib expressed deep grief over the passing of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali.
In a posting on his official social media page, Ramli and his wife, Toh Puan Raja Noora Ashikin Raja Abdullah, extended their heartfelt condolences to former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and his family.
"My wife and I express our deepest sorrow and pray that her soul be blessed with mercy, forgiven of all shortcomings, and placed among His righteous believers.
"May Allah grant the family strength, fortitude and patience in enduring this immense loss," he said.
Meanwhile, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow also extended his heartfelt condolences to the family of the late Dr Siti Hasmah.
Expressing deep sadness on behalf of the Penang government, Chow said her passing left behind an enduring legacy that would continue to inspire future generations.
"Truly, the passing of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah leaves behind a legacy that will continue to live .on, serve as an inspiration and be remembered by generations to come," he said.
Chow said his thoughts and prayers were with the bereaved family during this difficult time.
"To the entire family, we pray that they are granted strength, fortitude and continuous patience in facing this deeply challenging moment," he said.
Dr Siti Hasmah, a pioneering Malaysian woman doctor and wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, died at the age of 100.
She
died at the National Heart Institute
(IJN) this morning, with her death confirmed by her son, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir.
She is survived by her husband and seven children.

Title: Thai court dismisses petition challenging legality of 2026 election
Article:
BANGKOK: Thailand's Constitutional Court on Monday dismissed a petition challenging the legality of February's general election, ruling that the ballot papers used did not violate voter secrecy.
Nearly 38 million Thais voted in the Feb 8 election, which was won decisively by Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's Bhumjaithai Party, allowing it to form a coalition government controlling more than 290 of the 500 seats in parliament.
The ruling averts the possibility of an election re-run and will be welcomed by Anutin, whose party is facing a challenge to win public trust amid a stuttering economy and allegations of corruption and involvement in rigging a selection process for the Senate, which it denies.
The decision had been closely watched in Thailand, where the Constitutional Court has been at the heart of two decades of intermittent political turmoil through verdicts that dissolved big parties, voided two general elections and brought down multiple governments and prime ministers.
The court case stemmed from a petition filed by the ombudsman that argued that barcodes and QR (quick response) codes printed on ballot papers could be used to identify which candidate and party a voter chose.
The Election Commission had said the codes were used for security purposes and that identifying a voter would require access to ballot stubs that were stored separately.
The judges said that although barcodes on some ballots could potentially have been used to identify voters, they were included only for management purposes by election officials, with no intent to trace individual votes.
They said the arrangements for storing ballots, stubs and voter lists were "sufficiently safe".
The court nevertheless recommended against using such codes in future elections.
The same court voided a 2006 general election after finding the arrangement of polling booths compromised ballot secrecy and that the election had been called at too short notice.
It also annulled a 2014 election after anti-government protesters blocked some polling stations in Bangkok and the south, preventing voting from being held nationwide on the same day.
Those rulings both took place during periods of political tumult that led to military coups in the same year.

Title: Over 2,000 gather to pay final respects to Siti Hasmah
Article:
SERDANG: More than 2,000 congregants gathered at Masjid As Syarif, Taman Sungai Besi Indah this afternoon to perform funeral prayers for Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali.
The funeral prayers were performed twice, with the first led by Ustaz Muhammad Danial Hussan and the second by family representative Ustaz Basyir.
The prayers were completed at about 5.15pm.
The large congregation comprised family members, political leaders, friends and the public who gathered to pay their final respects to Dr Siti Hasmah, who
died
at the National Heart Institute (IJN) at 9.20am today.
The mosque was filled with a sombre atmosphere as mourners gathered for the funeral prayers for the deceased.
Following the prayers, a vehicle carrying her husband, former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, was seen leaving the mosque at about 5.20pm.
The remains of Dr Siti Hasmah were subsequently taken to the National Cemetery in Precinct 20, Putrajaya, where she will be laid to rest under the State Funeral of a National Dignitary accorded by the government.
Earlier, the public began arriving at the mosque as early as 1pm to pay their final respects, while political leaders, senior government officials and prominent figures also gathered at the mosque.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri
Anwar Ibrahim
and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, arrived at about 4pm, while former prime ministers Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob were among other political leaders present.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan were also among those who paid their respects.

Title: Malaysia's financial markets remain orderly amid global headwinds: Bank Negara
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's domestic financial markets continued to adjust in an orderly manner, supported by balanced two-way flows that ensured effective price intermediation among market participants, according to Bank Negara Malaysia's Financial Markets Committee (FMC).
The 'Discussion Summary' of the FMC Meeting 2/2026 revealed that market conditions remained conducive for corporates to raise funds to meet their financing requirements.
"Looking ahead, external factors such as geopolitical uncertainties, oil price volatility and an evolving global interest rate environment remain near-term headwinds for the domestic market. However, members noted that the recent increase in bond yields may present an attractive entry point for foreign investors, given that investor sentiment towards Malaysia continues to be favourable," the FMC said.
It added that these factors, alongside ongoing measures such as the qualified resident investor programme and engagement with government-linked companies, government-linked investment companies and corporates to repatriate and convert their foreign currency income, are expected to provide continued support for the foreign exchange and bond markets.
The FMC also said recent movements in the domestic financial markets were driven primarily by global factors, particularly developments in the US policy rate.
"Growing prospects of higher US interest rates and the actual realisation of a rate hike by the US Federal Reserve led to a stronger US dollar and higher US Treasury yields. These, in turn, resulted in broad-based adjustments across global markets, including regional currencies and bonds," it added.
On the currency, it noted that the ringgit moderated in September after remaining largely stable in July and August, while Malaysian Government Securities yields also increased following a prolonged period of relative stability. This came amid a broader repricing of global interest rate expectations and higher global bond yields.
Members of the committee also observed robust interest in corporate bond issuance and increased hedging activity.

Title: [UPDATED] Siti Hasmah's remains leave mosque for burial at National Cemetery
Article:
SERDANG: The remains of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali left Masjid As Syarif, Taman Sungai Besi Indah, this evening for the National Cemetery in Precinct 20, Putrajaya.
The remains were taken from the mosque following funeral prayers after Asar.
More than 2,000 congregants gathered at the mosque for the funeral prayers for the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.

Dr Mahathir was also at the mosque for the funeral prayers and was seen leaving about 5.20pm.
The vehicle carrying the remains was accompanied by vehicles carrying family members, political leaders and close friends.
A sombre atmosphere prevailed at the mosque as members of the public, family members, political leaders and prominent figures gathered to pay their final respects.
Members of the public began arriving as early as 1pm.
Among those present were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, who arrived about 4pm.
Former prime ministers Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin and Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob were also among the political leaders who came to pay their final respects.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil were also present.
Earlier, Anwar announced that Dr Siti Hasmah would be accorded a state funeral following her death.
The Prime Minister's Department subsequently announced that she would be accorded the State Funeral of a National Dignitary.
Dr Siti Hasmah, 100, died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) at 9.20am today. Her death was confirmed by her son, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir.
Her remains are being taken to the National Cemetery in Precinct 20, Putrajaya, where she will be laid to rest.

Title: ERS Energy crosses 1.5GWh BESS milestone
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ERS Energy Sdn Bhd says it has surpassed 1.5 gigawatt-hours (GWh) in cumulative utility-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity across Southeast Asia.
Most of the portfolio were secured over the past 12 months, the company said in a statement.
The milestone includes a 520 megawatt-hour (MWh) BESS project for ACEN in Zambales, Philippines, as well as two projects totalling 800MWh secured under Malaysia's inaugural Battery Energy Storage Programme (MyBeST).
ERS Energy said the projects strengthen its expansion beyond solar engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning into utility-scale energy storage development and system integration.
The company said its BESS projects are aimed at supporting grid stability and managing the intermittency of renewable energy as clean power deployment accelerates across Southeast Asia.
"Surpassing 1.5GWh of energy storage capacity is a tremendous testament to our team's execution discipline and the trust placed in us by our partners, lenders and regional grid operators," managing director Jonathan Kan said.
He said the milestone demonstrated the company's ability to translate energy policy ambitions into operational grid infrastructure.
ERS Energy said it is pursuing further opportunities in Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam and Australia, where increasing renewable energy penetration is driving demand for grid flexibility and energy storage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fugro deploys autonomous underwater vehicle for Petronas ultra-deepwater survey
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Fugro has completed a geohazard site survey commissioned by Petronas Carigali Sdn Bhd for the Megah and Limbayong fields off Sabah, supporting the development of Malaysia's offshore resources.
The survey provided critical geophysical data on seabed and subsurface conditions to identify potential hazards and support engineering design and field development planning in the ultra-deepwater environment.
The project marked the use of autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) technology for a Petronas Carigali ultra-deepwater geohazard survey.
Fugro deployed its Echo Surveyor 8 AUV from the Fugro Equator to collect high-resolution bathymetric, geophysical and shallow subsurface data while operating close to the seabed.
The campaign, which began in June and was completed in August 2026, was supported by Fugro's Kuala Lumpur Remote Operations Centre, which provided continuous data quality control and processing.
Fugro said the use of AUV technology and remote operations enabled faster data delivery and more efficient survey execution.
"By integrating advanced technologies with real-time remote operations, we enable faster insights and more efficient execution," said Safri Drahman, Asia Pacific regional business line director for marine site characterisation at Fugro.
He said the project demonstrated Fugro's continued investment in technology and its ability to deliver offshore solutions across the Asia Pacific region.

Title: Police freeze 5 bank accounts in Mandiri probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have frozen five bank accounts in connection with their investigation into Mandiri Development Centre Sdn Bhd (Mandiri), but have not disclosed the amount involved.
Bukit Aman Anti-Money Laundering Criminal Investigation Unit chief Datuk Fazlisyam Abdul Majid said investigations were ongoing, with several more individuals to be called to have their statements recorded.
"So far, five bank accounts belonging to parties under investigation have been frozen," he said when contacted today.
Fazlisyam did not disclose the value of the accounts or specify how many individuals had given statements so far.
Previously, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail was reported to have said that an investigation paper was opened on Sept 10 following a report concerning the receipt of funds suspected to be proceeds from illegal activities between 2024 and 2026.
The case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLATFPUAA).
The investigation covers the storage, transfer and use of funds, as well as the deposit or withdrawal of money suspected to be linked to proceeds from unlawful activities.
On Sept 22, Mandiri executive director Amir Hariri Abdul Hadi and finance director Dobby Chew were arrested after being called in by police to have their statements recorded in connection with the investigation.
They were subsequently remanded for three days to assist investigations before being released at 11.50pm last Thursday.

Title: Siti Hasmah once dreamt of being a journalist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Long before she became known as the woman beside a prime minister, a young Hasmah Mohd Ali of Klang dreamt of becoming a journalist.
But life took her down a different path, and the young lady who would eventually become known as Tun Dr Siti Hasmah would instead go on to make history herself.
She died at the age of 100, leaving behind a legacy deeply rooted in Malaysias rural communities. She was not only a devoted spouse, but a pioneering doctor who helped transform public health.
Medicine wasn't her first love, but it became her life's masterpiece.
In 1947, she entered Singapores King Edward VII College of Medicine as the only Malay woman among a largely male student body.
She didn't just survive a gruelling curriculum. She shattered the expectations of a deeply patriarchal era and went on to become one of the nation's earliest female doctors.
But her true calling wasn't found in gleaming hospital corridors. It waited for her in the sun-baked, remote villages of Kedah.
There, she saw the devastating toll of preventable illness and death. Mothers and infants were suffering, caught in a web of poverty, traditional taboos, and a sheer lack of medical knowledge.
The threat of childhood killers like polio, tuberculosis, and diphtheria constantly hung over these communities.
Dr Siti Hasmah didn't wait behind a desk for patients to find her. She went out to find them.
Trading the sterile comfort of a clinic for the muddy paths of the kampung, she brought vaccines, basic health education, and a fierce, maternal compassion directly to the people.
Rather than fighting local traditions, she worked alongside them. She trained traditional village midwives in modern safety practices so they could confidently protect mothers and newborns.
Because she bothered to listen and connect, rural communities finally learnt to trust modern medicine. Infant mortality rates plummeted.
Her empathy carried her to the global stage  from championing rural women's rights in Geneva to walking the volatile streets of Iraq in 2001, determined to check on children suffering under heavy economic sanctions.
Yet, back home, she remained grounded. She was often seen courtside supporting Malaysian badminton players, many of whom affectionately called her ibu (mother).
Dr Siti Hasmah was more than a medical trailblazer. For generations of Malaysians, particularly women and children in rural communities, her work helped bring healthcare closer to home.
In her later years, she humbly stated that she had nothing to leave the people except 'my love and my advice'. But looking at the generations of mothers and children who survived because she cared enough to walk into their villages, she clearly left much more.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former Negri exco members face more than 60 questions from Bukit Aman
Article:
SEREMBAN: More than 60 questions were posed to 10 former Negri Sembilan executive councilors today as Bukit Aman recorded their statements over the state's constitutional crisis.
Former state Industry, Technology, Innovation and Digital exco Datuk Mohd Asna Amin said the questions focused mainly on the ongoing crisis, with each exco member's statement recorded separately in sessions lasting between 30 and 35 minutes.
"Many Bukit Aman officers came, but none of them were intimidating, and we fully cooperated. For now, they are only recording our statements.
"More than 60 questions were asked and answered, all relating mainly to the crisis that is unfolding. Negri Sembilan is unique because its state constitution is different from those of other states.
"The Negri Sembilan State Constitution 1959 (UUTKNS) serves as the guide. We answered based on what we know," he told reporters at the tower's lobby here today.
Asna, who is also Lenggeng assemblyman, said they were informed that the statement-recording exercise could also involve other officials who may be called in.
He said Bukit Aman would inform them if further statements were required.
"We were informed that follow-up statements would be recorded if necessary," he said, adding that the authorities had not specified any particular provisions under which the statements were being recorded.
The statements are believed to be linked to the state's political crisis following the
revocation of the 10 exco members'
appointments by Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
The revocation came a week after the exco members issued a joint statement allegedly confirming Tuanku Muhriz's removal as state ruler.
The Negri Sembilan palace previously said the exco members had breached their oath of office and allegiance to the ruler, which they swore on Aug 7.
On Thursday, Ismail said the 10 former exco members, whom he maintained still legally held office,
had been barred
from entering their respective offices.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Dusuki Mokhtar had earlier affirmed that the revocation of the exco appointments, seven of whom are from Umno, was valid.
Yesterday, it was reported that the exco members would have their statements recorded.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail had previously said
Bukit Aman officers
would travel to Negri Sembilan to record their statements.
The 10 former exco members comprise Umno representatives Datuk Mustapha Nagoor (Palong), Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli (Linggi), Datuk Zaiful Bahri Idris (Chembong), Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali (Sungai Lui), Datuk Asna Mohd Amin (Lenggeng), Siti Nur Umaira Hasim (Labu) and Suhaimizan Bizar (Gemencheh).
The other three are MCA representative Siow Kong Choon (Chennah), Pas representative Fairuz Isa (Serting) and Wawasan representative Datuk Razali Abu Samah (Sikamat).
The session did not involve Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rapid KL vows cooperation in probe of bus crash that killed foreign student
Article:
SUBANG JAYA: Rapid KL has confirmed that one of its buses was involved in a crash along Persiaran Subang Permai here that killed a 19-year-old foreign student this morning.
It said the bus, operating on route T776 (USJ 7 Station-Subang Mewah), was travelling towards Subang Mewah at 6.19am when it collided with several vehicles parked on the road shoulder.
"A motorcycle at the location was also involved in the incident, leaving its rider and pillion rider injured.
"An ambulance arrived at the scene at 7.07am, after which medical personnel confirmed that one of the victims had died while the other was taken to Sungai Buloh Hospital for further treatment," it said in a statement.
Rapid KL said it would cooperate with authorities in their investigation into the incident.
Subang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat had said the bus was driven by a 29-year-old local man and was travelling from Persiaran Subang Mewah towards Edumetro when the driver was believed to have
lost control of the vehicle
.
He said the bus first crashed into the motorcycle, which was stopped at a red traffic light, before hitting a car parked on the left road shoulder and two other vehicles in front of it.
He said the motorcycle rider, a 19-year-old foreign student, suffered serious injuries and was taken to Shah Alam Hospital, while the 19-year-old pillion rider was pronounced dead at the scene.
Both victims were students at a private university in the Klang Valley.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: India's top court says need to fix accountability over Delhi rape cases
Article:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court of India on Monday pushed for accountability over a recent spate of rape cases in the national capital and neighbouring districts, saying they reflected a "failure of law enforcement", local media reported.
Hundreds of students protested in Delhi last week demanding better safety for women after a teenager said she was gang-raped by three men at a park in the city.
Last month, a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped in a moving bus by the driver and conductor, local media reported.
The Supreme Court said public spaces, including parks and buses, could not become "high-risk" zones because of poor lighting and surveillance, and other basic facilities, legal news website Live Law reported.
The court said fixing accountability was necessary and directed its administration to file a public interest petition on the issue for the court to pursue, legal news website Bar and Bench said.
Sexual violence is a major problem across India, with more than 80 rapes reported to police every day, according to the National Crime Records Bureau.
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta told a TV channel last week that there had been lapses and vowed to improve security, while Delhi Police said it had increased "visible policing" and intensified patrolling.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreign student killed as bus crashes into four vehicles in Subang Jaya
Article:
SUBANG JAYA: A 19-year-old foreign student was killed after a bus crashed into four other vehicles at Jalan USJ 1 here this morning.
The victim, a private university in the Klang Valley, was a pillion rider on a motorcycle with another 19-year-old foreign student when the accident occurred at 6.34am.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said the bus, driven by a 29-year-old man, was travelling from Persiaran Subang Mewah towards Edumetro when the driver is believed to have lost control of the vehicle.
"The bus first crashed into the motorcycle, which was stopped at a red traffic light, before hitting a car parked on the left road shoulder and two other vehicles in front of it.
"The pillion rider was pronounced dead at the scene, while the motorcycle rider suffered serious injuries and was taken to Shah Alam Hospital for treatment," he said in a statement today.
The deceased was taken to the Shah Alam Hospital Forensic Department for a post-mortem.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act for causing death by reckless or dangerous driving.
Those with information on the incident can contact investigating officer, Inspector Mohd Faizul Ahmad Suhaimi, from the Subang Jaya district police headquarters Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department at 019-475 7385.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Crowds gather at mosque for Siti Hasmah's funeral prayers
Article:

Members of the public began arriving at the mosque as early as 1pm, ahead of the funeral prayers for the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.

Title: Singapore-registered Audi investigated for dangerous driving on NSE
Article:
MUAR: Police are investigating two drivers, including the driver of a Singapore-registered Audi, for flashing strobe lights and driving dangerously on the North-South Expressway near yesterday.
A three-minute video showed the two drivers cutting in front of each other while using strobe lights, potentially putting other road users at risk.
The Singapore-registered Audi allegedly activated its strobe lights after the car behind flashed its high beams while attempting to overtake.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz said investigations revealed that the incident occurred at 5.48am yesterday at Km135 (southbound).
He said after the footage went viral, police lodged a first information report with its traffic division.
"Police have identified one of the vehicles, while efforts are ongoing to trace the other. We are also working to identify the owners and drivers of both vehicles to assist investigations," he said in a statement today.
Raiz Mukhliz said the case was being investigated under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless and dangerous driving.
The offence carries a maximum five-year jail term and a fine of between RM5,000 and RM15,000 upon conviction.
Federal Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Mohammed Hasbullah Ali said a police report was lodged by an officer from the district Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Division at 11.04am today after the viral Facebook video was detected.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Perak seeks RM1.4b in Budget 2027 for key water infrastructure
Article:
IPOH, Sept 28 — Perak is hoping for at least RM1.4 billion in the upcoming Federal Budget to fund key water supply infrastructure, particularly a project to transfer water from Sungai Perak to Bukit Merah to support farmers regularly affected by drought.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said the project was among the state’s priorities submitted by the Perak Economic Planning Unit to the Finance Ministry ahead of the Budget announcement.
“We are currently in the phase of realising the project to transfer water from Sungai Perak to Bukit Merah. If there is surplus water later, only then will we consider selling treated water to Penang.
“This is expected to help meet water needs in Kerian Integrated Green Industrial Park in northern Perak, including for farmers who, as we know, face problems every time there is a drought,” he said.
Saarani said this in a press conference when asked about state government’s wish list ahead of Federal Budget, at the launching of the 2MW Biogas Renewable Energy Plant at the Lahat Sanitary Landfill here.
Saarani said the project was expected to be operational by around 2030 or 2031 if it proceeded according to schedule.
“Hopefully, it will be included in this year’s Budget,” he said.
He said the project would involve two main components, with the first involving infrastructure such as pumps and water tunnels.
“This infrastructure should be funded by the Federal Government through the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry, with the necessary infrastructure works falling under the federal government’s responsibility through National Water Services Commission,” he said.
Saarani said the second component could be financed through Khazanah Air Perak, a consortium involving the state government and a subsidiary of the Perak State Agricultural Development Corporation.
“We can use loans, either from the federal government, through private finance initiative financing or from banks.
“But this can only be done once the infrastructure is in place,” he said.
Saarani said the infrastructure was crucial as the state had already identified the route for transporting water from Sungai Perak.
“We need pumps to draw the water and tunnels to transport it. This is expensive and needs to be started. That is the most important thing for us,” he said.
He said the estimated cost for the infrastructure alone was between RM1.4 billion and RM2 billion, excluding other components of the project.
“The longer we delay, the more expensive the materials will become,” he said.
Meanwhile, Saarani said the state government had also identified several urgent needs involving schools during a recent state development meeting.
He said one of the immediate concerns was the need for additional buildings at existing schools where six- and seven-year-old pupils would be entering Year One simultaneously next year.
“Therefore, there is a need to construct additional buildings,” he said.
Saarani said another concern involved dilapidated school buildings, with the state government receiving complaints from school principals and parent-teacher associations.
“There are many buildings that are already in poor condition, and this is beyond the capacity of the state government,” he said.
He said Perak also needed new schools in areas experiencing rapid development, particularly new growth areas.
“Whenever new development projects take place, there will be a need for new housing areas. Every new housing development should provide a location for a school.
“Schools are very important. We do not want schools operating in two sessions. We want single-session schools and schools that provide a comfortable environment for students to learn,” he said.
